briefings.title: AI and Jobs Series: What one company stopped doing - an HR exec weighs in
briefings.tldr: As AI automates rote tasks, organizations must transition from static job descriptions to fluid, skill-based roles while intentionally reinvesting saved time into high-value human relationships and strategic "unlearning."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
As AI automates rote tasks, organizations must transition from static job descriptions to fluid, skill-based roles while intentionally reinvesting saved time into high-value human relationships and strategic "unlearning."

## AI Implementation and the "Top of License" Philosophy
Cassandra Pratt, CHRO of Progyny, emphasizes that AI transformation is not about replacing workers, but about redistributing tasks to enhance professional fulfillment and efficiency.

*   **Work to the Top of Your License:** This guiding principle, used particularly with Progyny’s clinicians, encourages employees to spend more time on complex, high-level intellectual tasks while delegating administrative burdens—like note-taking or data entry—to AI agents.
*   **Tiered Rollout Strategy:** Progyny introduced AI through a structured roadmap:
    *   **Personal Productivity:** Initial focus on individual efficiency gains.
    *   **Custom Agents:** Transitioning toward building specialized agents and sharing prompts across teams.
    *   **Scheduled Training:** Clearly outlining what will be learned in specific quarters (e.g., Q1 vs. Q2) to prevent employee overwhelm.
*   **The 5% Efficiency Goal:** The company anticipates gaining 5% of staff time back initially through AI, with expectations for that number to grow to 15–20% as implementation matures.

## The "Unlearn" Framework and Meeting Culture
Drawing on Barry O’Reilly’s book *Unlearn*, Progyny utilizes a "Start, Stop, Continue" framework to sharpen execution and reduce burnout.

*   **The "Stop" Priority:** Leaders identified operational items and project reflexes that did not move the business forward.
*   **Meeting Discipline:** Progyny implemented a "No Agenda, No Meeting" policy.
    *   **Agenda Requirements:** Must include context, goals (brainstorming vs. decision-making), and participant roles.
    *   **Empowerment:** Employees are permitted to decline meetings that lack a well-formed agenda.
*   **Collaborative Problem-Solving:** Pratt noted a shift in workplace behavior: instead of "dropping a problem" on a colleague’s desk, employees now use AI for preliminary research to bring more well-formed positions to subject matter experts.

## Fluid Job Design and the Rise of the Generalist
The traditional, static job description is becoming obsolete in an era where AI-driven workflows evolve rapidly.

*   **Skill-Based Fluidity:** Job design is shifting from fixed responsibilities to matching specific employee skills with immediate business needs.
    *   **Dialogue:** Leadership must maintain open communication to reassure employees that shifting job descriptions signify positive growth rather than role elimination.
*   **The Generalist Advantage:** Pratt argues that while specialists remain valuable, "generalists will be the kings of the AI era" because they can connect dots across silos and package AI-generated insights for various audiences.
*   **Skills Mismatch:** Pratt expressed skepticism about "fixing" the skills mismatch entirely, noting that the rapid pace of AI means training must become an ongoing, experiential process rather than a one-time fix.

## Building "Superfans" Through Human Connection
As AI takes over technical work, Progyny is reinvesting human time into building deeper relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

*   **Superfans Strategy:** Employees are encouraged to use time saved by AI to understand their "audience" (clients, investors, or colleagues) more deeply.
*   **Spotlighting Humanity:** Progyny hosts "Spirit Weeks" and "Critical Impact Awards" to showcase employee "crafts"—ranging from painting and yoga to technical skills like Canva—to foster genuine human bonds that machines cannot replicate.
*   **Intentional Engagement:** Pratt recommends a "walking around" strategy for leaders to maintain physical human connection in a hybrid world, prioritizing active listening over transactional project updates.

## Strategic Well-being and Future-Proof Benefits
Progyny views comprehensive benefits not as "add-ons," but as critical components of a high-performance culture.

*   **Niche Support:** The company pioneered pregnancy loss leave in 2021 and offers specific support for parents with infants in the NICU.
*   **Catastrophic Leave:** A flexible leave type designed to support employees during major life traumas that exceed standard 30-day or 90-day policies.
*   **Financial ROI:** Pratt warns companies against cutting well-being benefits, noting that neglecting mental and physical health leads to higher medical claims and lost productivity that far exceed the cost of the benefits themselves.

> "AI allows us to make work like play... you can really focus on the things that people do best, which is building relationships, being creative, stimulating your intellect." — **Cassandra Pratt**

> "AI shouldn't be making the decision. It should be helping you compile the trends and the data so that then the human can read through it and make the appropriate decision." — **Cassandra Pratt**

> "I think even in the AI world, you need generalists who can connect the dots across many different areas of the business and help people understand all the different decision-making points before they move forward." — **Cassandra Pratt**

briefings.title: Builders Unscripted: Ep. 5 - Derya Unutmaz

people.name: Derya Unutmaz
people.role: Immunologist and Professor, The Jackson Laboratory

briefings.tldr: Immunologist Derya Unutmaz leverages advanced AI models like OpenAI's reasoning models and Codex to build custom biological software apps, simulate complex cellular immune responses, and pioneer a future of AI-driven personalized medicine.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Immunologist Derya Unutmaz leverages advanced AI models like OpenAI's reasoning models and Codex to build custom biological software apps, simulate complex cellular immune responses, and pioneer a future of AI-driven personalized medicine.

## Background & AI Adoption in Science
* **Early AI Inspiration:** Dr. Unutmaz first became interested in artificial intelligence during medical school in the early 1990s after realizing the overwhelming complexity of biological systems (trillions of parts and billions of reactions).
* **The Reasoning Breakthrough:** 
  * The transition to reasoning models (specifically *o1-preview* in September 2024) marked the definitive moment he realized AI was inevitable for science, noting its deep, insightful immunological responses compared to earlier iterations like GPT-4.
  * More recent models like GPT-5.5 Pro crossed a major threshold by successfully predicting complex experimental outcomes with 100% accuracy, matching his 30 years of laboratory intuition.

## Building Biological Tools with Codex
* **The "Codex Addict" Routine:** Waking up early with coffee, Dr. Unutmaz uses Codex to rapidly prototype software ideas, applications, and simulations, often running code overnight.
* **Custom Flow Cytometry App:** 
  * Built a fully working native macOS app using Swift and Codex to process flow cytometry data (single-cell fluorescent markers).
  * The software analyzes nearly 100,000 events, generates contour plots, and assists in designing specific antibody panels for identifying T cells (such as CD4 and CD8 killer cells).
* **CRISPR Gene-Editing Application:**
  * Created an application to target genes (like the CD4 gene) by pulling sequences from databases, evaluating 22-nucleotide target regions, ranking them, and designing multi-gene CRISPR libraries.

## Simulating Biological Systems & Digital Twins
* **T-Cell Receptor Simulator:** Built an interactive browser simulator modeling complex T-cell receptor signaling pathways, ligand affinities, doses, and phosphorylation patterns of transcription factors to predict cell survival, tumor clearance, or autoimmune response.
* **Interactive Immune Atlas:** 
  * Used Image 2.0 to generate a complex image based on a *Nature* journal immune atlas cover page.
  * Fed the image into Codex to build an interactive simulation website showing cellular interactions, checkpoint inhibitors (like the PD-1 molecule), and age-related immune behavior.
* **The Digital Twin Vision:** 
  * Aims to build complete "virtual cells," simulated immune systems, tissue models, and ultimately digital twins of individual human beings combining genetics, metabolites, gut bacteria, and hormones.
  * Predicts this will enable 100% effective, zero-side-effect personalized medicine and accelerate clinical trials from 5–10 years down to 5–10 days.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Derya Unutmaz** predicts that within the next 5 to 10 years, compute capabilities and AI will advance enough to successfully simulate complete biological systems.
* **Derya Unutmaz** predicts that within 15 years, humanity will achieve reverse aging, enabling people to live hundreds of years.
* **Derya Unutmaz** predicts that clinical trials will be accelerated from 5 to 10 years down to 5 to 10 days as AI takes over simulation-based testing.

## Notable Quotes
> "Before that, you know, GPT 4.0... it wouldn't really give you that kind of a deep, insightful, response. And, yeah, I still remember that day that was, you know, special."
> — Derya Unutmaz

> "What 5.5 did was almost as if it had the same experience that I had working in the lab for 30 years because there are certain things that are intuition."
> — Derya Unutmaz

> "The way we do science is going to completely change. The days where we would, for example, come up with an idea, plan for experiments for weeks and then analyze them for months, those days are over."
> — Derya Unutmaz

briefings.title: President Trump Participates in the Launch of Trump Accounts
briefings.tldr: President Trump and top financial and corporate leaders launched "Trump accounts" in the Oval Office—a new program providing every newborn American child with a $1,000 seed contribution and corporate backing to build an ownership economy through equity markets.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
President Trump and top financial and corporate leaders launched "Trump accounts" in the Oval Office—a new program providing every newborn American child with a $1,000 seed contribution and corporate backing to build an ownership economy through equity markets.

## Trump Accounts Launch & Mechanics
* **Program Overview:** Designed to give children born with no money a head start in equity markets by age 18.
  * **Current Sign-ups:** 6 million American children already signed up, with 86% coming from families earning less than $200,000.
  * **Initial Funding:** The US Treasury deposited one-time seed contributions of $1,000 into over 500,000 children's accounts.
  * **Corporate & Philanthropic Contributions:** $800 million in new capital will be invested this week through individual contributions and seed funds.
* **Key Corporate Backers:**
  * **Michael and Susan Dell:** Contributed $6.25 billion to fund 25 million eligible American children born between 2006 and 2024.
  * **Micron:** Contributed $250 million.
  * **State/Philanthropic Adoptions:** Indiana is adding $250 to all kids under five; Ray Dalio is contributing in Connecticut; specific schools and clubs are being adopted in San Francisco, Oakland, Durham, Philadelphia, and Newark.

## Stock Exchanges & Financial Leadership
* **Historic Joint Event:** The New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ held their first-ever joint opening bell-ringing ceremony, hosted in the Oval Office.
* **Key Officials & Executives:**
  * **President Trump:** Highlighted the administration's economic milestones, including the Dow hitting 50,000 and the S&P hitting 7,000 in record time.
  * **Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent:** Praised for central-casting execution and accelerating the initiative.
  * **Senator Ted Cruz:** Commended for championing the legislative process and pushing for the 70 million children target.
  * **SEC Chairman Paul Atkins:** Notified that accounts will show exact fractional ownership of major companies rather than generic index funds via a QR-code app designed by Joe Gebbia and the National Design Studio.
  * **Exchange Leaders:** Jeffrey Sprecher (Chairman/CEO, NYSE), Lynn Martin (President, NYSE), Adena Friedman (Chair/CEO, NASDAQ), and Nelson Griggs (President, NASDAQ).

## Economic Policies & Manufacturing Boom
* **Domestic Production:** $19.2 trillion in capital is driving record factory, plant, AI, and automotive manufacturing construction across the US.
* **Tariff Impact:** Foreign automakers (Japan, South Korea, Germany) and companies moving out of Canada and Mexico are building plants in the US to avoid tariffs.
* **Energy & AI Infrastructure:** The administration is granting fast approvals for dedicated electric-generating plants (including nuclear) to power the massive energy demands of AI data centers.

## Foreign Policy & Geopolitics
* **Ukraine/Russia War:** President Trump reported having a good call with President Putin and President Zelensky, expressing optimism that the war involving 25,000 to 36,000 monthly casualties is nearing an end.
* **Iran Conflict:** The administration reported completely destroying Iran's naval fleet (159 ships at the bottom of the sea), eliminating its radar and air force, and stopping all blockade-running oil shipments.

## Sports & Cultural Highlights
* **World Cup & Soccer:** President Trump discussed speaking with FIFA President Gianni Infantino regarding the successful US World Cup tournament and successfully petitioning for a review of a controversial red card issued to a top player, arguing players must compete at full strength.
* **White House Helipad:** A new granite White House helipad bearing the presidential seal is being constructed and fully paid for by Sikorsky due to the high-powered Marine One helicopters damaging the South Lawn grass.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Capital Growth & Scale:** Senator Ted Cruz claimed that over the next 12 months, corporate leaders, small business leaders, and philanthropists will raise over **$100 billion** for America's kids.
* **Long-Term Asset Accumulation:** Senator Ted Cruz claimed that over the next 15 years, over **$2 trillion** will go into the pockets of kids and families that would have otherwise had zero.
* **Total Child Coverage:** Senator Ted Cruz stated the goal to secure accounts for every single child in America—all **70 million kids** under the age of 18.
* **Market Outlook:** President Trump predicted that the stock market is "going to go through the roof when all those factories open" and that the country hasn't seen the biggest boom yet.

## Notable Quotes
> "The American dream belongs to every child and today we are equipping the next generation with the right to claim their rightful share of it." 
> — **Scott Bessent**

> "Today, we're pledging our fortune to the next generation of of children. So, to tens of millions of American children, your American story starts now." 
> — **Michael Dell**

> "Trump accounts are in many way Donald Trump's New Deal. But instead of having government taking care of everyone, Trump accounts are about making every child and every American a capitalist." 
> — **Senator Ted Cruz**

briefings.title: This CEO Raised $400 Million To "Poison" Your Data (And Protect Your Privacy) | The Under 30 Podcast
briefings.tldr: Arjun Bhatnagar, CEO of Cloaked, has raised $400 million to pioneer "data poisoning," a privacy strategy that uses masked, unique credentials for every transaction to disrupt the ability of AI and data brokers to track individual identities.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Arjun Bhatnagar, CEO of Cloaked, has raised $400 million to pioneer "data poisoning," a privacy strategy that uses masked, unique credentials for every transaction to disrupt the ability of AI and data brokers to track individual identities.

## The Core Philosophy: Data Poisoning
* **The Vulnerability of a Single Number:** Bhatnagar highlights that a single phone number can reveal an individual's Social Security number, address, family members, and credit card history because it acts as a universal identifier.
* **The "Poisoning" Strategy:** Rather than just deleting old data, Cloaked "poisons the well" by providing users with thousands of unique phone numbers, emails, and credit cards.
    * **Disrupting Identity:** By giving different information to every merchant (e.g., Domino’s vs. Sephora), there is no clear consensus for surveillance systems to build a profile.
    * **Contextual Relevance:** Data brokers value current, contextual data; Cloaked renders this data useless by ensuring it doesn't map back to a central identity.
* **The Privacy Paradox:** Bhatnagar notes that "people like to feel known, but they don't want to feel surveilled," aiming to balance personalization with safety.

## Product Capabilities and Security Infrastructure
* **Three-Pillar Protection:** The platform is designed to manage the full lifecycle of personal data:
    1. **Clean up the Past:** Scanning the dark web and removing existing data.
    2. **Defend the Present:** Using AI agents to screen calls; 40% of the millions of calls Cloaked handles daily are identified as AI scams.
    3. **Protect the Future:** Generating real-time masked credentials (emails, phone numbers, credit cards, and soon physical addresses).
* **Technical Architecture:** To prevent a mass breach, Cloaked does not use a single "multi-tenant" database.
    * **Unique Infrastructure:** Every user has their own unique database and infrastructure.
    * **Zero-Knowledge Encryption:** The company cannot access user data; even if the system is breached, an attacker would have to hack every individual user's encrypted database separately.
* **Financial Services Integration:** Cloaked allows users to create merchant-specific credit cards with hard spending limits (e.g., a card exclusively for Spotify capped at $15/month).

## Explosive Business Growth and Market Scale
* **Funding Milestones:** The company has raised over **$400 million**, including a $375 million Series B in 2024.
* **User Adoption:** 
    * **Consumer Base:** Grown from 20,000 to nearly 400,000 paying subscribers in approximately one year.
    * **Pricing Model:** Primarily B2C, with users paying roughly $10/month or $100/year.
    * **Enterprise Shift:** Expanded from zero to over 50 enterprise accounts in four months, driven by employees wanting the tool for business use.
* **Strategic Partnerships:** 
    * **NFLPA Partnership:** Cloaked has a deal to provide privacy services to every NFL athlete to protect them from doxing, physical threats, and financial fraud.
    * **Sports as a Standard:** After working with the Chicago Cubs, Cloaked views professional sports as the "gold standard" for testing high-stakes security.

## Founder Insights: High-Stakes Leadership
* **The $1.5M Marketing Gamble:** In late 2023/early 2024, Cloaked was nearly out of cash. Bhatnagar decided to spend the final $1.5 million on performance marketing to prove the "story" of their growth. The gamble worked, leading to their massive Series B.
* **Storytelling Over Decks:** Bhatnagar advises young founders to "ditch the deck." He practiced by sending voice memos to investors while driving, refining his ability to explain the AI privacy crisis without visual aids.
* **AI Origin Story:** The idea for Cloaked began in 2020 when Bhatnagar built a personal AI that accidentally began "automating" his relationship, sending "I love you" texts and memes to his girlfriend without his knowledge. This made him realize the terrifying lack of control individuals have over personal data used by AI.

> "I realized the question of security and privacy and personal data will be the biggest question of our lifetime when AI comes to life. Now, surprise, we're exactly in that world." — **Arjun Bhatnagar**

> "People like to feel known, but they don't want to feel surveilled... what we really want to accomplish is to make those statements true, so you can keep living your life, but there's Cloaked in the middle saying, 'Let’s figure out how this data should look.'" — **Arjun Bhatnagar**

> "One investor gave me this advice: ditch the deck and tell the story." — **Arjun Bhatnagar**

briefings.title: Who Wins the Midterms & What It Means for Markets with Dan Clifton | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 67
briefings.tldr: The 2026 midterm elections are trending toward a split government with Democrats favored to flip the House, while the Federal Reserve prepares for a "regime change" under Kevin Warsh focused on shrinking the $6 trillion balance sheet rather than immediate rate cuts.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The 2026 midterm elections are trending toward a split government with Democrats favored to flip the House, while the Federal Reserve prepares for a "regime change" under Kevin Warsh focused on shrinking the $6 trillion balance sheet rather than immediate rate cuts.

## The 2026 Midterm Landscape
*   **Trump’s Approval Rating:** Currently sits at 38%. Clifton notes that Trump’s approval on the economy went negative for the first time in April 2025 following tariff proposals, turning a former political asset into a liability.
*   **The House of Representatives:** Democrats only need a net gain of three seats to take control. Clifton predicts they will likely succeed, transitioning the midterms into a referendum on the incumbent.
*   **The Senate Battle:** Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats for total control (or three if they hold the VP tie-breaker). 
    *   **North Carolina:** Likely to flip to Democrats due to a popular former Democratic governor running.
    *   **Maine:** Market odds give Democrats a 60% chance to flip Susan Collins' seat, though her incumbency remains a formidable obstacle.
    *   **Ohio and Texas:** Expected to be highly competitive and expensive races, though Republicans remain slight favorites to hold.
    *   **The "Powell Factor":** Fed Chair Jerome Powell may delay his departure until after the midterms; if Democrats win the Senate, Trump would be forced to appoint a mainstream economist rather than a "MAGA" candidate for the role.

## The "Warsh Fed" and Monetary Policy
*   **Balance Sheet Focus:** Kevin Warsh is prioritizing shrinking the Fed’s $6 trillion balance sheet over interest rate adjustments. The goal is to reduce the money supply—which leads goods inflation by approximately 15 months—to eventually allow for lower rates.
*   **Privatizing Reserves:** The strategy involves "privatizing" the Fed balance sheet by easing bank regulations (e.g., liquidity coverage ratios), encouraging private banks to hold more Treasuries and absorb the liquidity currently provided by the Fed.
*   **Market Resilience:** Despite expectations shifting from rate cuts to a possible 25-basis-point hike, the market has remained resilient because the broader economy is stronger than anticipated.

## Tariffs and Fiscal Stimulus
*   **Headwind to Tailwind:** While tariffs were a market drag in early 2025, they have become a tailwind. The effective tariff rate dropped from 11% in October to 7% today.
*   **Net Fiscal Impact:** The U.S. has collected only $35 billion in net tariff revenue year-to-date while distributing $75 billion in corporate tax cuts and tariff refunds. 
*   **Currency Strategy:** The next phase of "Trump 2.0" trade policy likely involves an aggressive push to lower the value of the U.S. dollar to boost the impact of domestic investment incentives.

## The 2028 Presidential Outlook
*   **Democratic Frontrunners:** Gavin Newsom is the current betting favorite, followed by Pete Buttigieg, who is viewed as a "fighter" by the base. Other contenders include Governors Josh Shapiro (PA), Gretchen Whitmer (MI), and Wes Moore (MD).
*   **Republican Field:** 
    *   **J.D. Vance:** Has a significant head start because Trump is not restricting his campaign activities.
    *   **Marco Rubio:** Seen as a "superstar" who can articulate Trump’s foreign policy to the establishment, though his standing is tied to the success of the Iran conflict.
    *   **Ron DeSantis:** Remains highly active on national issues and is positioning himself for a populist run centered on affordability.

## Emerging Risks: AI Backlash and Regional War
*   **Data Centers as "The New Fracking":** Clifton warns of a growing political backlash against AI data centers due to their massive consumption of land, water, and electricity.
    *   **The Local Trade-off:** In Loudoun County, VA, data centers pay 40% of the education bill, saving average residents $2,500 a year in property taxes—a "public good" narrative the tech industry has yet to master.
*   **The Iran Conflict:** The war is proving unpopular with Trump’s base, who expected an "anti-war" presidency. 
    *   **Oil Prices:** The U.S. and China are both tapping reserves to keep gas below $5.00/gallon to prevent a political breaking point.
    *   **Defense Shift:** The conflict is accelerating a shift in investor preference toward "Defense Tech" (drones/software) over traditional large-cap hardware providers.

***

> "Trump turned his greatest asset, his strength on the economy, into a liability [with the 2025 tariff proposals] and that’s driven down his overall approval rating." — **Dan Clifton**

> "What Warsh is literally arguing is that we're making a policy choice to have a large balance sheet and high interest rates... we need a lower balance sheet. When we get that, then we can actually start to get rates lower." — **Dan Clifton**

> "Data centers are the new fracking. It’s the same environmental money being used to oppose them, and the technology industry is behind the ball on the politics." — **Dan Clifton**
